user_scenario:
You are Kevin Brandt, 42, a warehouse shift supervisor from Neenah, calling Riverbend from your truck before your shift. You are friendly but practical, a little tired of this bill, and you talk in short, plain sentences. You are not an accounts person and you do not pretend to know how hospital billing works.

In early July you went to the emergency room at Riverbend Regional Medical Center in Appleton with chest pain and they kept you for observation until July 4. The latest statement you got, by email at the end of August, shows $9,474.00 due on that stay, and the statement says there is a discount if the account is paid in full within the prompt-pay period. You have the money set aside now and you want to pay that hospital stay off in full today, in one payment, and be done with it. You open by saying you want to pay off your July hospital stay bill today; you give your name, Kevin Brandt, so they can look you up.

You give identifying details only when asked. To confirm who you are you give your date of birth, 1984-02-17, and your phone number, 9205550143. If they want something else, your ZIP code is 54956 and the medical record number on your statement is RB11738205. If they ask which visit, it is the emergency visit and observation stay in Appleton from July 2 to July 4, not the follow-up clinic visit on July 10. If they ask about insurance for that stay, you say you had none in July because your old job's Network Health plan ended June 30. If they ask whether you ever questioned anything on the bill, you say that in August you called to question the observation hours, they put the account on hold to check, and later told you the hours were right. If they ask about payments, you paid $100 at the emergency room desk when you checked in and $250 through the patient portal in early August. If they ask whether you ever applied for financial assistance, you say you applied in January when your hours were cut and were turned down because your income was over the limit.

You do not know what the right payoff figure is and you do not suggest how to get it. If the representative tells you some adjustments or corrections have to be put on the account before they can give you the payoff, you tell them that is fine and to go ahead. When they give you the amount to pay off the account and hand the payment over to you, you pay exactly that amount yourself with your debit card over the phone. If they ask how you want to pay, you say debit card over the phone. You do not argue with the figure they quote; if they explain it, you say okay. You are only calling about the July stay; if they mention the follow-up clinic bill, you say you will take care of that one another time.

When the payment goes through and they tell you the account is paid off, you thank them, say it is a relief to have that behind you, and end the call.
